title: Introduce TF orchestrator with subnet-claim fencing and immutable-iam profiles
author: Juniper Lee
release_notes: Add `tf-orchestrator` to coordinate atomic applies across tenant state backends; introduce subnet-claim fencing to avoid double-allocation of subnets during parallel upgrades; add immutable IAM profiles for tenant-scoped roles to reduce drift during rollbacks. Backwards-compatible rollout with feature flag and migration tool included.
description:
Motivation and context:
Customers running Redwood Private reported two recurring problems during upgrades: (1) concurrent terraform applies against per-tenant state caused transient double-allocation of (small) subnets and IAM race conditions; (2) rollbacks after partial failures frequently exposed IAM role drift which made re-apply brittle. This PR introduces a lightweight tf-orchestrator module plus two supporting modules/patterns to mitigate these classes of failures for GPU-backed private deployments.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds modules/tf-orchestrator: a small coordinator that sequences terraform operations per-tenant and provides a pluggable lock/fencing backend (DynamoDB-style lease by default, noop for air-gapped installs). It exposes pre-apply and post-apply hooks for canary tasks (helm chart preflight, kube-object reconciliation).
- Introduces modules/subnet-claim-fence: a claim interface and terraform helper that atomically allocates subnet IDs with a fencing token. Prevents two controllers from claiming the same /28-/24 in racey upgrade scenarios.
- Adds modules/immutable-iam-profile: a pattern that creates immutable role ARN prefixes and rotation-safe attachment objects so rollbacks do not re-use rotated names and cause dangling grants.
- Updates modules/gpu-nodepool to emit tenant-scoped node pool names and to accept an external "fence_token" output to bind with claim flow.
- Migration tool: scripts/migrate-orchestrator.sh and a step-by-step doc to move existing per-tenant state into orchestrator-managed apply order.

Why this design:
- Minimize blast radius: orchestrator sequences changes per-tenant while keeping terraform state boundaries intact (we do not collapse state files).
- Compatible with air-gapped installs: fencing backend is pluggable; default uses a small DynamoDB table but the module supports filesystem- or consul-backed implementations for on-prem.
- Safe rollbacks: immutable IAM profile naming reduces identity churn when a prior release rolls back and later re-applies.

Review conversation (condensed):
- Marcus Chen: "This looks good overall. Two asks: (1) make fence backend pluggable in examples; (2) include a conservative default lock TTL so long-running applies don't leak."
- Juniper Lee: "Addressed: added backend variable with example consul fs implementation + default ttl of 15m and an explicit renew script for long applies. Pushed commit cf8b2e7."
- Evelyn Park: "Immutable ARN pattern is helpful. Please ensure IAM policies referencing dynamic ARNs are computed via outputs so external infra doesn't rely on ephemeral names."
- Juniper Lee: "Updated outputs to include stable_role_arn and stable_role_id; documented migration caveat for existing policies in runbook."
- Diego Morales: "Integration tests flaked once due to timing. Added jitter and retry to claim helper; re-ran CI."

CI / checks summary:
- terraform validate (modules) : pass
- unit tests (claim tests) : pass
- integration (concurrent apply harness) : pass after one retry
- linters (tflint, tfsec) : pass (one minor tfsec suppression for allowed broad assume-role for control-plane bootstrapping)

Migration and rollout notes:
- The orchestrator is opt-in. To adopt, teams run scripts/migrate-orchestrator.sh which takes current per-tenant state buckets and registers them with the orchestrator control table. The runbook includes a dry-run mode and a checklist to run canary applies on a single tenant before full conversion.
- Backwards compatibility: existing Terraform state layout is preserved; orchestrator only sequences applies. If the orchestrator is removed, state remains untouched.

Operational considerations and follow-ups:
- We should add a Prometheus exporter for claim-fence metrics (allocations, conflicts) in a follow-up PR (tracked ENG-5527).
- Add a Helm chart preflight hook that validates fence-token reachability during preflight (follow-up).

Merge outcome:
- PR merged via squash on 2025-12-01 after full approvals and green CI. Post-merge: created a short-lived feature-flagged rollout to enable orchestrator in staging, validated four rolling upgrades using the new flows and confirmed no subnet collisions and stable IAM roles across rollbacks.

If you want to run this locally: see modules/tf-orchestrator/README.md for quickstart and scripts/migrate-orchestrator.sh for migration steps.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: it sequences applies rather than consolidating state files, reducing risk for customers with complex per-tenant TF state. The fencing and immutable name patterns were co-designed with SRE to reduce incident recurrence during private upgrades.
